headline: GENESIS-VAULT SEAL A$12.6bn DEAL — 700,000 oz Australian Gold Giant Born From Bidding War; Beats Regis At 14.5% Premium, A$2bn Synergies Forecast (ASX:GMD / ASX:VAU)
snippet: Genesis Minerals and Vault Minerals agreed on July 14 to merge in a scheme of arrangement valuing Vault at A$12.6 billion — Australia's largest gold M&A deal of 2026 — capping a bidding war that saw Genesis outmanoeuvre Regis Resources at a 14.5% premium over Regis's offer price. Under the terms, Vault shareholders receive 0.7629 Genesis shares plus A$0.475 cash per share, with Genesis shareholders retaining 59.8% of the combined group; the merged entity will produce 600,000–700,000 ounces annually from Western Australian operations, hold 33.6 million ounces of mineral resources and 9.4 million ounces of ore reserves, and capture an estimated A$2 billion in post-tax synergies over 10 years through the proximity of Leonora and Bardoc-Mount Monger operations. Vault will pay Regis a A$50.7 million break fee.

headline: AUSTRALIA STRIPS VOTING RIGHTS OF THREE CHINA-LINKED NORTHERN MINERALS SHAREHOLDERS — Chalmers Freezes 12.96% Stake After Divestment Defiance (ASX:NTU)
snippet: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers issued an interim direction on July 14 stripping voting and other shareholder rights from three China-linked entities — Hong Kong Ying Tak Ltd., Real International Resources Ltd. (BVI), and Qogir Trading and Service Co. Ltd. (Hong Kong) — after they failed to comply with a May 2026 government order to divest their stakes in rare earths developer Northern Minerals Ltd. by July 2. The three entities collectively hold 12.96% of Northern Minerals, which is advancing its Browns Range heavy rare earths project in Western Australia; the action marks an escalation in Australia's critical-minerals sovereignty campaign as Canberra blocks offshore interests from gaining effective control of strategic assets.

headline: OROSUR'S APTA FIRES: 135.5m AT 1.91 g/t Au — High-Grade Core Hits 26m AT 7.15 g/t, 13.8m AT 12.73 g/t; Drill Terminated Early In Broken Ground Still In Mineralization (TSXV:OMI)
snippet: Orosur Mining Inc. (TSXV: OMI) announced July 14 that drill hole MAP107 at the APTA target within the Anzá project in Colombia returned a composite intersection of 135.5 metres at 1.91 g/t gold from 111.65 metres depth — including a high-grade sub-interval of 49 metres at 4.06 g/t, 26 metres at 7.15 g/t, and 13.8 metres at 12.73 g/t — after the hole encountered the Aragon fault zone mineralization much shallower than predicted by historical drilling. The hole was terminated early in broken ground yet remained in mineralization, indicating the deeper high-grade APTA zone may be more laterally extensive than modelled; results will guide geological reinterpretation that could support a future Mineral Resource Estimate if follow-up drilling justifies it.

headline: WEST POINT GOLD PUSHES NE TYRO TO 350m DEPTH — Arizona Gold Chain Returns 51.9m AT 2.5 g/t Au Including 21.4m AT 4.72 g/t; Maiden Resource Estimate Due Later 2026 (TSXV:WPG)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / West Point Gold Corp.
snippet: West Point Gold Corp. (TSXV: WPG) reported July 14 assay results from five drill holes (1,542 metres) at the high-grade Northeast Tyro zone on its Gold Chain Project in Arizona — including hole GC26-169 returning 51.9 metres at 2.50 g/t gold from 276 metres, with an embedded 21.4-metre interval at 4.72 g/t and an estimated true width of 38 metres. The results push the NE Tyro zone to at least 350 metres depth where it remains open both at depth and to the northeast toward the untested Frisco Graben target; 14 holes totalling 4,378 metres from the recently completed 21,079-metre campaign still await assay, with all results to feed a maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate expected in late 2026.

headline: SPANISH MOUNTAIN GOLD EXPANDS ORCA FAULT: 80.15m AT 0.83 g/t — Including 27.2m AT 1.92 g/t; Seven-Hole Batch From Cariboo's Largest Open-Pit Gold Feasibility Program (TSXV:SPA)
snippet: Spanish Mountain Gold Ltd. (TSXV: SPA) reported July 14 assay results from seven diamond drill holes at its Spanish Mountain Gold Project in the Cariboo Gold Corridor, British Columbia, as part of its 2026 Feasibility Study drill program — headlined by hole 26-DH-1376, which returned 303.18 metres at 0.50 g/t gold, including an upper high-grade interval of 80.15 metres at 0.83 g/t gold with an embedded 27.2-metre zone grading 1.92 g/t gold. The 2026 feasibility program targets both resource infill to improve geological confidence and expansion drilling; Spanish Mountain holds one of the largest gold deposits in the Cariboo region and is advancing toward a feasibility study supporting a potential large-scale open-pit operation.

headline: U.S. DOE LICENSES SEAWATER URANIUM EXTRACTION TO SUPERCRITICAL — Exclusive PNNL Adsorbent Tech Targets 4.5 Billion Tonnes In World's Oceans; Former National Lab Scientists Lead Commercialization
snippet: SuperCritical Materials secured an exclusive U.S. Department of Energy licence on July 14 to commercialize patented adsorbent technology developed at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory that extracts uranium — and other critical materials — from seawater, with exclusive U.S. rights preceding international deployment into allied countries. The company notes the world's oceans contain approximately 4.5 billion tonnes of uranium, more than 1,000 times identified land-based reserves, offering a theoretically limitless feedstock for nuclear fuel; CEO Alexander Canon Bryan is positioning SuperCritical as critical supply infrastructure for what he calls the
as AI and advanced manufacturing drive surging baseload power demand. Co-founder Gary Gill was a leading PNNL seawater uranium researcher.

headline: VANECK: DPM METALS BEATS Q2 GOLD OUTPUT BY 31% — Vares Shutdown Done In 7 Days vs 20 Planned; Global Central Bank Buying Hit 41 Tonnes In May, Highest Since November 2025
snippet: VanEck's weekly Gold SWOT analysis published July 13 highlights that DPM Metals (formerly Dundee Precious Metals) exceeded its Q2 2026 gold production estimate by 31%, driven primarily by stronger-than-expected throughput at the Vares silver-zinc-lead mine in Bosnia, where the planned plant maintenance shutdown was completed in just seven days against a 20-day schedule — a significant operating efficiency beat. The piece also flags that global central bank gold demand accelerated sharply in May, reaching 41 tonnes of net purchases, the highest monthly total since November 2025, with Poland leading at 18 tonnes, as institutions continue building gold reserves against currency debasement and geopolitical uncertainty.

headline: OREZONE'S FIRST FULL CASA BERARDI QUARTER 'IN LINE WITH EXPECTATIONS' — H2 2026 Weighted To Q4 As P17 Pit Grade Ramps; Bomboré-Quebec Multi-Mine Model Now Operating (TSX:ORE)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Orezone Gold Corporation
snippet: Orezone Gold Corporation (TSX: ORE) reported July 14 its Q2 2026 production results — the company's first full quarter as a multi-mine producer since completing the Casa Berardi acquisition — with both the Bomboré mine in Burkina Faso and the Casa Berardi underground mine in Quebec performing in line with expectations. Production is weighted toward H2 2026 with Q4 expected to be the strongest quarter as ore deliveries from the higher-grade P17 pit increase; Orezone sold 1,625 ounces in Q2 under Casa Berardi's streaming agreement at 20% of spot gold price, with Q2 financial results expected after market close on August 12.

headline: CANALASKA'S NEBULA WINTER DRILL CONFIRMS BASEMENT ALTERATION — Graphitic Fault Zones + Hydrothermal Alteration In Athabasca Basin; 30km From Key Lake, Saskatchewan (TSXV:CVV)
snippet: CanAlaska Uranium Ltd. (TSXV: CVV) announced July 14 results from its Nebula winter drill program in the southeastern Athabasca Basin, Saskatchewan, confirming the presence of strongly graphitic pelite with re-activated cross-cutting fault zones carrying hydrothermal alteration — classic structural precursors to basement-hosted unconformity uranium deposits of the type that define the Athabasca's high-grade district. The 100%-owned Nebula project is located approximately 30 kilometres southwest of Cameco's past-producing Key Lake mine and the currently operating Key Lake Mill, placing any discovery within direct proximity of one of the world's largest uranium processing facilities.
